name: Admin team dashboard
description:
1. **Request:** the board (kanban/sprint) had to respect the "chat belongs to one project" constraint in multi-project views — use the project when the board is scoped to one, ask the user when it spans several — reusing the existing QuickChat view.
2. **First delivery:** I built `BoardQuickChat.vue` + a floating assistant button and wired them into `KanbanBoardView.vue`, with the ProjectManager avatar and a changeable project tree selector.
3. **Correction:** you clarified the change belonged to the **Management Dashboard**, not the board views, so I reverted `KanbanBoardView.vue` and deleted the board-only components.
4. **Real gap found:** `ManagementDashboardView.vue` already had its own assistant panel with a hardcoded `AI` badge and no project control — my earlier component was never mounted there.
5. **Final state:** the dashboard's assistant now shows the ProjectManager avatar on the header button, the floating action and next to its name, plus an always-visible, changeable project selector (`ProjectDetailt`) that focuses the whole dashboard on the chosen project.

messages.content:
We must create a powerful admin team dashboard where show active work, status, blockers and expectations. 

First look must tell user if there's anything important urgent, the it can navigate and drill down on all elements to understand project's work, team, and task status.

Dashboard must be modern, will have left bar with navigation, mobile first. Interactive dashboards and AI assistant to answer any user's question.

Dashboard will show work status and tasks from all projects with time filter (last week as default) 

Dashboard is meant for management to understand what's going on, what has been done, stoppers, and delivery prevision.

Add cost analysis and AI consumption.

Dashboard will have different sections the user can access by the left bar.
Add filters to the different sections.

----
Work only with "api" and "client" folders, ignore others.
Review all existing dashboards and create a mockup @Mockups

```py api/codx/junior/model/planning.py
"""
Planning domain models.

Shared request/response models for the ``/api/planning/*`` surface. They are
consumed by:

    * ``POST  /api/planning/tasks/query``    -> PlanningTaskQueryResponse
    * ``POST  /api/planning/dashboard``       -> PlanningDashboardResponse
    * ``GET   /api/planning/activity``        -> List[ActivityEvent]
    * ``PATCH /api/planning/tasks/{task_id}`` -> PlanningTaskUpdateResponse
    * ``POST  /api/planning/tasks/reorder``   -> PlanningReorderResponse

All dataset-wide aggregation, filtering and sorting is performed by
:class:`codx.junior.planning_manager.PlanningManager`, so the numbers the UI
renders are always computed over the *entire* filtered dataset instead of a
single loaded page.
"""

from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class PlanningRange(BaseModel):
    """
    Date window applied to a configurable field.

    ``from`` is a reserved Python keyword, so the attribute is named ``from_``
    while the JSON alias stays ``from`` for clients (and the JS
    ``PlanningQuery`` model). ``populate_by_name`` keeps ``from_`` accepted too.
    """
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    field: str = Field(
        default="updated_at",
        description="Which date the range applies to: updated_at | due_date | created_at",
    )
    from_: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None, alias="from", description="Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD"
    )
    to: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None, description="Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD"
    )


class PlanningSort(BaseModel):
    """Sort configuration applied server-side before pagination."""
    field: str = Field(
        default="priority",
        description="sort_index | priority | due_date | updated_at",
    )
    dir: str = Field(default="asc", description="asc | desc")


class PlanningQuery(BaseModel):
    """Shared request for the planning list and the follow-up dashboard."""
    range: Optional[PlanningRange] = Field(default=None)
    boards: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default=None)
    assignees: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default=None)
    priorities: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default=None)
    statuses: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default=None)
    search: Optional[str] = Field(default=None)
    attention_only: bool = Field(default=False)
    include_done: bool = Field(default=True)
    include_templates: bool = Field(default=False)
    project_ids: Optional[List[str]] = Field(default=None)
    group_by: Optional[str] = Field(
        default="priority", description="priority | status | board | None"
    )
    page: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)
    page_size: int = Field(default=50, ge=1, le=100)
    sort: PlanningSort = Field(default_factory=PlanningSort)


class PlanningTask(BaseModel):
    """A single task row with server-computed derived flags."""
    id: str
    name: str = ""
    description: Optional[str] = None
    board: Optional[str] = None
    column: Optional[str] = None
    status: str = "todo"
    priority: str = "low"

Mock data for missing endpoints. Notify me when all is ready for testing.

I'll start by investigating the client structure, router, navigation (AppsSections) and the existing API surface so the new view integrates properly.Search results were unhelpful. Let me locate the actual files by pattern.The search tool is returning cached noise. Let me read the folder tree directly.Now let me read the router, AppsSection, and the API/store patterns I must follow.I have the full picture. I'll implement it as real client code: a `management` API module (mock-backed for the endpoints that don't exist yet), a composable holding state/aggregations, the view, and the registrations.

Let me write the API module first.Now the composable that owns state, filters and the derived aggregations:Now the view itself — shell (left rail, range filter, overlays) plus the six sections:Now registering the route:Now the app registry (so desktop mode opens it as a panel too):Finally, the navigation entry in `AppsSection`:Let me verify `AppRouteView` resolves the app key the way I registered it:Everything is implemented and registered. Here's the status in the standing format.

# TL; DR;

The management dashboard is **built, wired into the router and into the left navigation**, and ready for you to test. Nothing is a mockup screen any more — it's a real Vue view.

- Open it from the sidebar: **APPS → Management** (icon `fa-table-columns`), or go to `/<project-name>/management-dashboard`.
- On desktop it also opens as a **dockview panel**, so you can keep it next to the Task Manager.
- It has the six sections from the approved mockup (Pulse, Work, Blockers, Delivery, Team, Cost & AI), the time filter (**7d by default**), left rail, task/member drawers and the AI assistant.
- **What is still simulated:** boards, tasks, people and AI usage. Only the **project list is real** (`/api/projects`). That is by design — you asked for mock data for the missing endpoints — and it is isolated in one file so replacing it with real endpoints is a one-line change per call.
- **Decision needed from you:** which of the 6 proposed endpoints gets built first (see the last section).

---

## 1. Summary

Management asked for one screen that answers, at a glance: *is anything urgent, what is moving, what is stuck, who is loaded, what will it cost and when do we demo.* The screen exists now, in the client, behind the project shell, in both display modes.

## 2. What was built

| File | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `client/src/api/modules/management.js` | **new** | The dashboard's data contract. Real `GET /api/projects`, everything else generated deterministically (seeded) in the browser behind the exact async shape a backend would expose. |
| `client/src/views/management/useManagementDashboard.js` | **new** | Single source of truth: time range, per-section filters, lazy per-section loading, all aggregations, persistence of your last view, mutations + assistant. |
| `client/src/views/ManagementDashboardView.vue` | **new** | The screen: left rail (drawer when narrow), header with the range filter, the six sections, task drawer, member drawer, reassign modal, AI assistant, toasts. |
| `client/src/router/index.ts` | update | `/{projectName}/management-dashboard` → `name: 'management-dashboard'`, `meta.app` resolved by `AppRouteView`. |
| `client/src/config/apps.js` | update | `management-dashboard` app: desktop panel **and** mobile route. |
| `client/src/config/appComponentsMap.js` | update | Maps the key to the view (code-split, lazy). |
| `client/src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` | update | **APPS → Management** entry + handler. |

## 3. What you'll see (test checklist)

1. **Pulse (default)** — first look is the red strip: *"N things need you now"* with severity dots, the oldest blocker's age and a jump to Blockers. Below: 6 KPIs (Active / Blocked / Overdue / Completed / Demos / AI spend), "Delivering now" per board with ETA, "Needs attention", team load, activity feed, AI spend bars. Every block is clickable.
2. **Work** — project / board / status / priority / assignee filters, search, sortable columns, pagination. Table on wide panels, cards below 820px. Row → drawer.
3. **Blockers** — reason chips (Blocked / Overdue / Due today / Unassigned / Stalled) with counts, project filter, and per-item actions: Open, Ask for update, Reassign, Unblock.
4. **Delivery** — boards tracked, at-risk count, next demo, forecast card per board (progress vs target, velocity, ETA, confidence), burndown with board selector, milestones & demo table.
5. **Team** — capacity summary, filters (everyone / humans / AI agents, project, overloaded-only), member cards with load %, active/blocked/done and attributed AI cost → member drawer with their tasks.
6. **Cost & AI** — spend, tokens, cost per delivered task, weekly budget, projected week, avg per call; consumption chart with series toggles (Spend / Tokens / Calls), by project, by person, by model, per-project budget bars.
7. **Cross-cutting** — the range filter (**Today / 7d / 30d / 90d**, default 7d) applies to every section and survives a reload; assistant answers from the same data with source chips that navigate; `⋯ → Refresh` and `⋯ → Regenerate mock data`.

Things worth knowing while testing: the drawer edits (status, priority, due date, progress, assignee, unblock, mark done) **really write to the mock store** and the aggregates refresh, so you can demo a Blocker being cleared and watch the Pulse strip shrink. When a panel is narrow the rail becomes an off-canvas drawer — resizing a dockview panel is the fastest way to check mobile-first behaviour.

## 4. Dependencies & the endpoint contract to build next

The view only talks to `managementModule`, so shipping the real thing is a swap per method, not a rewrite:

| Proposed endpoint | Feeds | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/management/overview?from&to` | Pulse (all of it) | mock `overview()` |
| `POST /api/management/tasks/query` | Work (+ boards, people) | mock `tasks()` |
| `GET /api/management/blockers?from&to` | Blockers | mock `blockers()` |
| `GET /api/management/delivery?from&to&board_id` | Delivery + burndown | mock `delivery()` |
| `GET /api/management/team-load?from&to` | Team | mock `team()` |
| `GET /api/management/cost?from&to&project_id&model` | Cost & AI | mock `cost()` |
| `PATCH /api/management/tasks/{id}` | drawers / actions | mock `updateTask()` |
| `POST /api/management/assistant` | assistant | mock `ask()` |

The AI-cost numbers can already be served by the admin analytics endpoints that exist today (`/api/analytics/admin/total|daily|by-project|by-model|by-user`) — that's the cheapest first real slice.

## 5. Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-project work status has **no backend today** (planning reads `/api/chats/search`, which is project-scoped) | The Work/Blockers sections stay mocked until an aggregate endpoint exists | Scope the endpoint above as the first real slice; nothing in the view changes. |
| Mock numbers are deterministic, so they only move with the time window | A demo may look "frozen" | `⋯ → Regenerate mock data`, or move the range filter. |
| Real people/capacity are not in the mock roster | Team attribution is illustrative | Same swap: `team-load` returns real members. |
| Assistant answers are rule-based | It can't answer arbitrary questions yet | Clearly labelled; wires to a real assistant endpoint later. |

## 6. Decision needed from you

**Which endpoint do we build first?** Recommendation: `GET /api/management/overview` — it makes Pulse (the screen management will actually open) truthful across all projects, and it is the one they will demo to their own stakeholders. Decide-by: before we schedule the next increment; the fake-data caveat has to disappear from the header before this goes to management.

## 7. Next demo & checkpoint

- **Now:** you test the navigation entry and the six sections against the mock.
- **Then:** tell me which numbers look wrong or missing per section — that list *is* the endpoint contract, and I'll slice it into the next increment (each section is independently deployable/demoable).
- Note on the URL: it's `/{project-name}/management-dashboard`, not a bare `/management-dashboard` — the dashboard lives inside the project shell like every other screen, so the active project carries into it. If management needs a project-agnostic version (like `Solopreneur`), say so and I'll add it as an unscoped route.

 * One reactive object (`d`) is shared by the shell and by every section

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_tiktoken_available = False
try:
    import tiktoken
    _tiktoken_available = True
except ImportError:
    logger.warning("tiktoken not installed — using word-split token approximation")


def count_tokens(text: str, model: str = "gpt-4o") -> int:
    """
    Estimate the number of tokens in *text* for *model*.

    Uses tiktoken when available; falls back to a rough word-split approximation
    (1 token ≈ 0.75 words) when tiktoken is not installed.

    Args:
        text:  The text to measure.
        model: Model name used to select the correct encoding in tiktoken.

    Returns:
        Integer token count estimate.
    """
    if not text:
        return 0

    if _tiktoken_available:
        try:
            encoding = tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model)
        except KeyError:
            # Unknown model — fall back to cl100k_base (GPT-4 family default)
            encoding = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return len(encoding.encode(text))

    # Fallback: 1 token ≈ 4 characters (common rule of thumb)
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)

# TL; DR;

**The dashboard is not "fake" any more — it has a real backend contract.** Two of the six sections get **genuinely live data on day one** (Work / Blockers / Team come from the real task boards of every project you can see; Cost & AI comes from the real token-usage store). The other two are live but **structurally incomplete**, and it is important management knows why before they see it:

- **Delivery cannot show a date**, because sprint boards have **no target date and no demo date** in the data model. The forecast can show progress, velocity and a computed ETA — not "will we make the demo".
- **Team % load is approximate**, because tasks carry **no estimate field**. It is derived from active task count against a 40h week.
- **"Blocked" is a convention, not a field**: a task is blocked when its status is `onhold` (or it carries a `blocked:` tag). Nothing in the model records *why* it is blocked unless someone writes it in the tag.

Everything else is real: real projects, real boards, real tasks, real status history (the burndown is computed from actual `status_history` transitions), real token cost per project / person / model.

**Decision needed from you (2 items, both cheap):** add `target_date` + `demo_date` to the board model, and an `estimate_h` field to tasks. Those two fields are the difference between a dashboard that *informs* management and one that *predicts* for them.

Connecting the admin dashboard to the API means answering one question honestly: *what does the backend actually know?* I mapped the existing surface (`PlanningManager`, `Analytics`, `ChatManager`, kanban/task storage) and built the dashboard on the parts that exist, marking the rest explicitly.

**One new backend file, one new client file, one line changed in existing code.** Nothing else touched.

"""
Management dashboard router — cross-project view for management.
============================================================================

The screen answers one question, across EVERY project the caller can see and
for a time window: *what is happening, what is stuck, who is loaded and what
will it cost*.

Route layout
------------
GET   /api/management/overview          – everything the Pulse section draws
POST  /api/management/tasks/query        – filtered, sorted, paginated work
GET   /api/management/blockers           – the attention queue
GET   /api/management/delivery           – forecast + burndown per board
GET   /api/management/team-load          – capacity, workload and cost per person
GET   /api/management/cost               – spend, tokens, models and budget
PATCH /api/management/tasks/{task_id}    – update a task (POST is also accepted)
POST  /api/management/assistant          – answer a question over the live data

WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM
-------------------------
There is no new storage. Everything is read from what the platform already
persists, which is why the dashboard cannot drift from the kanban boards:

    * tasks      -> ``ChatManager(settings=project).list_chats()`` of every
                    project the caller has access to (a task IS a chat).
    * activity   -> ``<codx_path>/planning/events.jsonl`` (already event sourced).
    * burndown   -> ``Chat.status_history`` (append-only status transitions).
    * cost       -> the analytics store (``Analytics``, cxjcoins per request).

WHAT THE MODEL DOES NOT KNOW (read this before trusting a number)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
These are surfaced as ``null`` instead of being invented:

    * ``target_date`` / ``demo_date`` per board — the ``Kanban`` model has no
      such field, so a forecast can report ETA + velocity but NOT "will we make
      the demo".
    * ``estimate_h`` per task — tasks carry no estimate, so capacity uses
      ``DEFAULT_TASK_HOURS`` and the resulting ``load_pct`` is an APPROXIMATION.
    * ``blocked`` — there is no blocked flag. A task is considered blocked when
      its status is in ``BLOCKED_STATUSES`` (``onhold``/``blocked``) or when it
      carries a ``blocked:<reason>`` tag. The reason is only as good as the tag.

WINDOW RULE
-----------
A task belongs to the window when it was *updated* inside it **or** it is still
open. A blocker must never disappear because it stopped moving — that is the
whole point of the screen, and it is the one place where management semantics
deliberately differ from the project planning view.

CACHING
-------
Reading every project's chats means walking the filesystem per project, and the
API kills a request after ``GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`` (30s). The raw chat
load is therefore cached for ``CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`` per project set and dropped
on every write.

# ── Canonical values ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

PRIORITY_ORDER = ["high", "medium", "low"]
STATUS_ORDER = ["todo", "doing", "onhold", "done", "rejected"]

CLOSED_STATUSES = {"done", "rejected"}
ACTIVE_STATUSES = {"todo", "doing"}
BLOCKED_STATUSES = {"onhold", "blocked"}

DEFAULT_PRIORITY = "medium"
DEFAULT_STATUS = "todo"

#: A "doing" task not touched for this many days is surfaced as stalled.
STALLED_AFTER_DAYS = 21

#: How bad each attention reason is (drives ordering; higher = worse).
SEVERITY = {
    "blocked": 4.0,
    "overdue": 3.0,
    "due_today": 2.0,
    "unassigned_high": 1.5,
    "stalled": 1.0,
}

#: Palette used when a project has no colour of its own (stable per project id).
PROJECT_PALETTE = [
    "#e2419f", "#38bdf8", "#22c55e", "#f59e0b",
    "#a855f7", "#14b8a6", "#f05252", "#6366f1",
]

#: Capacity envelope used to turn "assigned work" into a percentage. Tasks do
#: not carry an estimate today, so both numbers are configuration, not data.
WEEKLY_CAPACITY_HOURS = float(os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_MANAGEMENT_CAPACITY_HOURS", "40"))
DEFAULT_TASK_HOURS = float(os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_MANAGEMENT_TASK_HOURS", "4"))

#: Weekly AI budget. Nothing stores it yet, so it is configuration.
WEEKLY_BUDGET_CXJCOINS = float(
    os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_MANAGEMENT_WEEKLY_BUDGET", "6000")
)

#: Seconds the raw per-project chat load is kept in memory.
CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = float(os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_MANAGEMENT_CACHE_TTL", "30"))

ATTENTION_LIMIT = 50
ACTIVITY_LIMIT = 30
DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS = 7


# ── Date helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _as_datetime(value: Any) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """Parse an ISO date/datetime string (or datetime) into a naive datetime."""
    if not value:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, datetime):
        return value.replace(tzinfo=None)
    text = str(value).strip()
    if not text:
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(text.replace("Z", "+00:00")).replace(tzinfo=None)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    try:
        return datetime.fromisoformat(text[:19])
    except ValueError:
        logger.debug("management: unparseable timestamp '%s'", value)
        return None


def _as_date(value: Any) -> Optional[date]:
    """Parse an ISO date/datetime string into a ``date``."""
    parsed = _as_datetime(value)
    return parsed.date() if parsed else None


def _today() -> date:
    return date.today()


def _today_iso() -> str:
    return _today().isoformat()


def _day_iso(value: date) -> str:
    return value.isoformat()


def _normalize_range(from_value: Optional[str], to_value: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """
    Normalize the requested window.

    Args:
        from_value: Inclusive start (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO datetime); optional.
        to_value: Inclusive end; optional.

    Returns:
        ``(from, to)`` as ISO dates. Defaults to the last 7 days.
    """
    end = _as_date(to_value) or _today()
    start = _as_date(from_value) or (end - timedelta(days=DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS))
    if start > end:
        start, end = end, start
    return _day_iso(start), _day_iso(end)


def _in_window(iso_value: Any, start: str, end: str) -> bool:
    """Whether an ISO timestamp falls inside the inclusive ``[start, end]`` day range."""
    day = str(iso_value or "")[:10]
    return bool(day) and start <= day <= end


def _window_days(start: str, end: str) -> int:
    """Number of days covered by the window (minimum 1)."""
    first, last = _as_date(start), _as_date(end)
    if not first or not last:
        return DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS
    return max(1, (last - first).days + 1)


def _pct(part: float, total: float) -> int:
    """Integer percentage, 0 when the denominator is empty."""
    return int(round((part / total) * 100)) if total else 0


# ── Project helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _project_color(project_id: str) -> str:
    """Stable colour for a project that does not define one."""
    total = sum(ord(char) for char in str(project_id or ""))
    return PROJECT_PALETTE[total % len(PROJECT_PALETTE)]


def _visible_projects(user: Optional[CodxUser]) -> List[Any]:
    """
    Projects the caller may see.

    Uses the same permission walk as ``GET /api/projects``, so the dashboard can
    never show work from a project the user cannot open.
    """
    if not user:
        return []
    try:
        projects = list(find_all_user_projects(user))
    except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - a broken project must not break the view
        logger.error("management: project discovery failed: %s", ex)
        return []
    return [project for project in projects if getattr(project, "project_id", None)]


def _project_index(projects: Iterable[Any]) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
    """``project_id -> {id, name, color}`` with the fallback colour applied."""
    index: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for project in projects:
        project_id = getattr(project, "project_id", None)
        if not project_id:
            continue
        index[project_id] = {
            "id": project_id,
            "name": getattr(project, "project_name", None) or project_id,
            "color": getattr(project, "project_color", None) or _project_color(project_id),
        }
    return index


def _project_users(project: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Usernames with access to a project.

    ``CODXJuniorProject.users`` is filled by the discovery step and holds plain
    usernames, but dicts are tolerated so a future shape change cannot break
    the roster.
    """
    usernames: List[str] = []
    for entry in getattr(project, "users", None) or []:
        if isinstance(entry, str):
            usernames.append(entry)
        elif isinstance(entry, dict):
            username = entry.get("username") or entry.get("email")
            if username:
                usernames.append(username)
        else:
            username = getattr(entry, "username", None)
            if username:
                usernames.append(username)
    return usernames


# ── Chat loading (cached) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_CHATS_CACHE: Dict[str, Tuple[float, List[Tuple[str, Chat]]]] = {}
_CACHE_LOCK = threading.Lock()


def _cache_key(projects: Iterable[Any]) -> str:
    ids = sorted(str(getattr(project, "project_id", "")) for project in projects)
    return "management:chats:" + ",".join(ids)


def _cache_get(key: str) -> Optional[List[Tuple[str, Chat]]]:
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        entry = _CHATS_CACHE.get(key)
        if not entry:
            return None
        created, value = entry
        if (datetime.now().timestamp() - created) > CACHE_TTL_SECONDS:
            _CHATS_CACHE.pop(key, None)
            return None
        return value


def _cache_put(key: str, value: List[Tuple[str, Chat]]) -> None:
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        _CHATS_CACHE[key] = (datetime.now().timestamp(), value)


def invalidate_management_cache() -> None:
    """Drop the cached chat load (called after every write)."""
    with _CACHE_LOCK:
        _CHATS_CACHE.clear()


def _load_chats(projects: Iterable[Any]) -> List[Tuple[str, Chat]]:
    """
    Read the chats of every project once.

    Returns:
        ``[(project_id, chat), ...]``. A project that cannot be read is logged
        and skipped so one broken project never blanks the dashboard.
    """
    rows: List[Tuple[str, Chat]] = []
    for project in projects:
        project_id = getattr(project, "project_id", None)
        if not project_id:
            continue
        try:
            manager = ChatManager(settings=project)
            for chat in manager.list_chats():
                rows.append((project_id, chat))
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - defensive: a project may be unreadable
            logger.warning(
                "management: cannot read chats of project '%s': %s",
                getattr(project, "project_name", project_id),
                ex,
            )
    return rows


def _all_chats(projects: Iterable[Any]) -> List[Tuple[str, Chat]]:
    """Cached version of :func:`_load_chats`."""
    projects = list(projects)
    key = _cache_key(projects)
    cached = _cache_get(key)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached
    rows = _load_chats(projects)
    _cache_put(key, rows)
    return rows


# ── Task projection ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _normalize_status(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    status = (value or "").strip().lower()
    return status if status in STATUS_ORDER else DEFAULT_STATUS


def _normalize_priority(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    priority = (value or "").strip().lower()
    return priority if priority in PRIORITY_ORDER else DEFAULT_PRIORITY


def _is_task(chat: Chat) -> bool:
    """
    Whether a chat should appear as a task.

    Mirrors the rule of the project planning view: templates are excluded, and
    a plain conversation only counts when it carries planning metadata.
    """
    if getattr(chat, "is_template", False):
        return False
    if (getattr(chat, "mode", None) or "chat") == "chat":
        return bool(
            (chat.status or "").strip()
            or (chat.priority or "").strip()
            or (chat.due_date or "").strip()
            or (chat.assignees or [])
        )
    return True


def _block_reason(tags: Iterable[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """Read the ``blocked:<reason>`` tag convention."""
    for tag in tags or []:
        text = str(tag or "").strip()
        if text.lower().startswith("blocked:"):
            return text.split(":", 1)[1].strip() or None
        if text.lower() == "blocked":
            return None
    return None


def _blocked_since(chat: Chat, blocked: bool) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    When the task entered a blocked status.

    Read from the append-only ``status_history`` so the age of a blocker is real
    data instead of the last modification date.
    """
    if not blocked:
        return None
    for event in reversed(list(chat.status_history or [])):
        if (event.to_status or "").strip().lower() in BLOCKED_STATUSES:
            return str(event.at or "")
    return str(chat.updated_at or "") or None


def _done_at(chat: Chat) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """When the task reached ``done`` (last transition, else ``updated_at``)."""
    for event in reversed(list(chat.status_history or [])):
        if (event.to_status or "").strip().lower() == "done":
            return _as_datetime(event.at)
    if _normalize_status(chat.status) == "done":
        return _as_datetime(chat.updated_at)
    return None


def _task_payload(chat: Chat, project: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Project a ``Chat`` into the shape the dashboard renders.

    Every derived flag is computed here, server-side, so the six sections and
    the assistant cannot disagree about what "overdue" means.
    """
    today = _today()
    status = _normalize_status(chat.status)
    priority = _normalize_priority(chat.priority)
    assignees = list(chat.assignees or [])
    tags = list(chat.tags or [])

    due = _as_date(chat.due_date)
    days_until_due = (due - today).days if due else None
    closed = status in CLOSED_STATUSES

    overdue = bool(due and days_until_due is not None and days_until_due < 0 and not closed)
    due_today = bool(due and days_until_due == 0 and not closed)
    unassigned = not assignees

    updated_at = _as_datetime(chat.updated_at)
    stalled = bool(
        status == "doing"
        and updated_at is not None
        and (datetime.now() - updated_at).days >= STALLED_AFTER_DAYS
    )

    blocked = status in BLOCKED_STATUSES or any(
        str(tag).strip().lower().startswith("blocked") for tag in tags
    )

    reason: Optional[str] = None
    if blocked and not closed:
        reason = "blocked"
    elif overdue:
        reason = "overdue"
    elif due_today:
        reason = "due_today"
    elif unassigned and priority == "high" and not closed:
        reason = "unassigned_high"
    elif stalled:
        reason = "stalled"

    board = (chat.board or "").strip() or "—"
    project_id = project["id"]

    return {
        "id": chat.id or chat.doc_id or "",
        "name": chat.name or "(untitled)",
        "description": chat.description or None,
        "project_id": project_id,
        "project_name": project["name"],
        "project_color": project["color"],
        "board_id": f"{project_id}:{board}",
        "board": board,
        "board_type": "kanban",
        "column": chat.column or None,
        "status": status,
        "priority": priority,
        "due_date": chat.due_date,
        "progress": int(chat.progress or 0),
        "assignees": assignees,
        "assignee_names": assignees,
        "assignees_info": [
            {"id": username, "name": username, "role": "Member", "type": "human"}
            for username in assignees
        ],
        "users": list(chat.users or []),
        "tags": tags,
        "mode": chat.mode or "task",
        "created_at": str(chat.created_at or ""),
        "updated_at": str(chat.updated_at or ""),
        # estimate_h is configuration until tasks carry an estimate field
        "estimate_h": DEFAULT_TASK_HOURS,
        "days_until_due": days_until_due,
        "overdue": overdue,
        "due_today": due_today,
        "unassigned": unassigned,
        "blocked": blocked,
        "block_reason": _block_reason(tags),
        "blocked_since": _blocked_since(chat, blocked),
        "attention_reason": reason,
        "severity": SEVERITY.get(reason or "", 0.0),
        "_done_at": _done_at(chat),
    }


def _window_tasks(
    projects: Iterable[Any],
    project_index: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]],
    start: str,
    end: str,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Every task of the window, in the dashboard shape.

    Window rule: updated inside the window **or** still open.
    """
    rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for owner_project_id, chat in _all_chats(projects):
        if project_id and owner_project_id != project_id:
            continue
        if not _is_task(chat):
            continue
        if not _in_window(chat.updated_at, start, end) and _normalize_status(chat.status) in CLOSED_STATUSES:
            continue
        project = project_index.get(owner_project_id)
        if not project:
            continue
        rows.append(_task_payload(chat, project))
    return rows


# ── Aggregations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _metrics(tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Headline metrics over the whole window."""
    by_status = {status: 0 for status in STATUS_ORDER}
    by_priority = {priority: 0 for priority in PRIORITY_ORDER}
    overdue = due_today = unassigned = blocked = 0

    for task in tasks:
        by_status[task["status"]] = by_status.get(task["status"], 0) + 1
        by_priority[task["priority"]] = by_priority.get(task["priority"], 0) + 1
        if task["overdue"]:
            overdue += 1
        if task["due_today"]:
            due_today += 1
        if task["unassigned"] and task["status"] not in CLOSED_STATUSES:
            unassigned += 1
        if task["blocked"]:
            blocked += 1

    done = by_status.get("done", 0)
    total = len(tasks)
    return {
        "total": total,
        "done": done,
        "active": by_status.get("todo", 0) + by_status.get("doing", 0),
        "on_hold": by_status.get("onhold", 0),
        "rejected": by_status.get("rejected", 0),
        "overdue": overdue,
        "due_today": due_today,
        "unassigned": unassigned,
        "blocked": blocked,
        "completion": _pct(done, total),
        "by_status": by_status,
        "by_priority": by_priority,
    }


def _board_progress(tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Per-board progress.

    ``board_id`` / ``id`` and ``board`` / ``name`` are both emitted because the
    board list is reused as a filter source by the Work section.
    """
    buckets: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for task in tasks:
        bucket = buckets.setdefault(
            task["board_id"],
            {
                "board_id": task["board_id"],
                "id": task["board_id"],
                "board": task["board"],
                "name": task["board"],
                "project_id": task["project_id"],
                "project_name": task["project_name"],
                "project_color": task["project_color"],
                "type": task["board_type"],
                "total": 0,
                "done": 0,
                "doing": 0,
                "todo": 0,
                "on_hold": 0,
                "overdue": 0,
                "blocked": 0,
                "unassigned": 0,
                # A board target date does not exist in the model yet.
                "target_date": None,
                "demo_date": None,
            },
        )
        bucket["total"] += 1
        if task["status"] == "done":
            bucket["done"] += 1
        elif task["status"] == "doing":
            bucket["doing"] += 1
        elif task["status"] == "todo":
            bucket["todo"] += 1
        elif task["status"] == "onhold":
            bucket["on_hold"] += 1
        if task["overdue"]:
            bucket["overdue"] += 1
        if task["blocked"]:
            bucket["blocked"] += 1
        if task["unassigned"] and task["status"] not in CLOSED_STATUSES:
            bucket["unassigned"] += 1

    boards: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for bucket in buckets.values():
        bucket["percentage"] = _pct(bucket["done"], bucket["total"])
        boards.append(bucket)
    boards.sort(key=lambda item: (item["project_name"], item["board"]))
    return boards


def _attention(tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """The attention queue, most severe first."""
    items = [
        {"task": task, "reason": task["attention_reason"], "severity": task["severity"]}
        for task in tasks
        if task["attention_reason"]
    ]
    items.sort(key=lambda item: (item["severity"], item["task"]["updated_at"]), reverse=True)
    return items[:ATTENTION_LIMIT]


def _activity(
    projects: Iterable[Any],
    task_ids: Optional[set] = None,
    limit: int = ACTIVITY_LIMIT,
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Merge the activity feeds of every project (newest first).

    Events live in ``<codx_path>/planning/events.jsonl`` and are written by the
    planning write endpoints, so the feed is an audit trail, not a guess.
    """
    events: List[Any] = []
    for project in projects:
        codx_path = getattr(project, "codx_path", None)
        if not codx_path:
            continue
        try:
            events.extend(PlanningEventStore(codx_path).read())
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - a missing store is not an error
            logger.debug("management: no planning events in %s: %s", codx_path, ex)

    if task_ids is not None:
        events = [event for event in events if event.target_task_id in task_ids]

    events.sort(key=lambda event: _as_datetime(event.timestamp) or datetime.min, reverse=True)

    return [
        {
            "id": event.id,
            "actor": event.actor,
            "actor_type": event.actor_type,
            "action": event.action,
            "task_id": event.target_task_id,
            "task_name": event.target_task_name,
            "target_task_id": event.target_task_id,
            "target_task_name": event.target_task_name,
            "board": event.board,
            "field": event.field,
            "from_value": event.from_value,
            "to_value": event.to_value,
            "timestamp": event.timestamp,
            "tone": event.tone,
        }
        for event in events[:limit]
    ]


def _forecast(tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]], start: str, end: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Per-board velocity and ETA.

    Velocity is measured inside the selected window (tasks closed per week),
    which is the only throughput signal the data actually provides. Because the
    board model carries no target date, ``status`` reports risk from blockers and
    overdue work — not "will we make the demo".
    """
    weeks = max(1.0, _window_days(start, end) / 7.0)
    boards = _board_progress(tasks)

    forecast: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for board in boards:
        done_in_window = len([
            task for task in tasks
            if task["board_id"] == board["board_id"]
            and task["status"] == "done"
            and task["_done_at"] is not None
            and start <= task["_done_at"].date().isoformat() <= end
        ])
        velocity = round(done_in_window / weeks, 1)
        remaining = max(0, board["total"] - board["done"])
        eta_days = int(round((remaining / velocity) * 7)) if velocity > 0 else None

        status = "on_track"
        confidence = "high" if velocity > 0 else "low"
        if board["blocked"] or board["overdue"]:
            status = "at_risk"
            confidence = "low" if board["blocked"] else "medium"
        if remaining and velocity == 0:
            status = "at_risk"
            confidence = "low"

        forecast.append({
            **board,
            "committed": board["total"],
            "remaining": remaining,
            "velocity": velocity,
            "eta_date": (_today() + timedelta(days=eta_days or 0)).isoformat() if eta_days is not None else None,
            "eta_days": eta_days,
            "confidence": confidence,
            "status": status,
        })
    return forecast


def _burndown(
    projects: Iterable[Any],
    project_id: Optional[str],
    board_id: Optional[str],
    days: int = 14,
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Burndown of one board, from real status transitions.

    The curve is rebuilt from ``Chat.status_history``: for every day of the
    window we count the tasks that were already ``done`` by the end of that day,
    so the line is history rather than an interpolation.
    """
    chats = [
        (owner, chat)
        for owner, chat in _all_chats(projects)
        if _is_task(chat)
        and (not project_id or owner == project_id)
        and (not board_id or f"{owner}:{(chat.board or '').strip() or '—'}" == board_id)
    ]
    if not chats:
        return None

    total = len(chats)
    points: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    today = _today()

    for offset in range(days - 1, -1, -1):
        day = today - timedelta(days=offset)
        done_by_day = 0
        for _, chat in chats:
            done_at = _done_at(chat)
            if done_at and done_at.date() <= day:
                done_by_day += 1
        ideal = max(0, int(round(total - (total / max(1, days - 1)) * (days - 1 - offset))))
        remaining = max(0, total - done_by_day)
        points.append({
            "date": day.isoformat(),
            "ideal": ideal,
            "actual": remaining,
            "remaining": remaining,
        })

    board_row = next(
        (row for row in _board_progress([
            _task_payload(chat, {"id": owner, "name": owner, "color": "#e2419f"})
            for owner, chat in chats
        ]) if row["board_id"] == board_id),
        None,
    )

    return {
        "board_id": board_id,
        "board": board_row["board"] if board_row else board_id,
        "total": total,
        "points": points,
    }


def _people(
    projects: Iterable[Any],
    tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]],
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    The roster: project users plus everybody who is assigned something.

    Ids are usernames because ``Chat.assignees`` holds usernames and the cost
    store groups by username — using a synthetic id would break the join.
    """
    people: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}

    def add(username: str, role: str = "Member") -> None:
        username = str(username or "").strip()
        if not username or username in people:
            return
        people[username] = {
            "id": username,
            "name": username,
            "role": role,
            "type": "human",
        }

    for project in projects:
        for username in _project_users(project):
            add(username)
    for task in tasks:
        for username in task["assignees"]:
            add(username)

    return sorted(people.values(), key=lambda person: person["name"].lower())


def _team_load(
    tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    people: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    cost_by_user: Dict[str, Any],
) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Capacity and workload per person.

    ``load_pct`` compares the estimated hours of the *open* work assigned to a
    person against a 40h week. Tasks have no estimate field, so the hourly
    figures use ``DEFAULT_TASK_HOURS`` — read the percentage as a signal, not as
    a commitment.
    """
    load: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for person in people:
        username = person["id"]
        mine = [task for task in tasks if username in task["assignees"]]
        active = [
            task for task in mine
            if task["status"] in ACTIVE_STATUSES or task["status"] == "onhold"
        ]
        hours = sum(task["estimate_h"] for task in active)
        usage = cost_by_user.get(username) or {}

        load.append({
            **person,
            "capacity_h": WEEKLY_CAPACITY_HOURS,
            "hours": round(hours, 1),
            "load_pct": _pct(hours, WEEKLY_CAPACITY_HOURS),
            "active": len(active),
            "blocked": len([task for task in mine if task["blocked"]]),
            "done": len([task for task in mine if task["status"] == "done"]),
            "overdue": len([task for task in mine if task["overdue"]]),
            "cost_cxjcoins": round(float(usage.get("total_cxjcoins") or 0), 2),
            "project_ids": sorted({task["project_id"] for task in mine}),
            "last_active": max(
                (task["updated_at"] for task in mine), default=None
            ),
        })

    load.sort(key=lambda row: row["load_pct"], reverse=True)
    return load


# ── Cost ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_analytics: Optional[Analytics] = None


def _get_analytics() -> Analytics:
    """Shared analytics store instance (same path the analytics router uses)."""
    global _analytics
    if _analytics is None:
        _analytics = Analytics(analytics_path=ANALYTICS_DATA_PATH)
    return _analytics


def _normalize_usage(raw: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Coerce an analytics usage dict into the keys the dashboard reads."""
    raw = raw or {}
    return {
        "input_tokens": int(raw.get("input_tokens") or 0),
        "output_tokens": int(raw.get("output_tokens") or 0),
        "total_tokens": int(raw.get("total_tokens") or 0),
        "calls": int(raw.get("calls") or 0),
        "total_duration_seconds": round(float(raw.get("total_duration_seconds") or 0), 1),
        "total_cxjcoins": round(float(raw.get("total_cxjcoins") or 0), 2),
    }


def _period_day(value: Any) -> str:
    """Normalize an analytics period (epoch, ISO datetime or date) to YYYY-MM-DD."""
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return datetime.fromtimestamp(value).date().isoformat()
    text = str(value or "")
    return text[:10]


def _cost_payload(
    projects: List[Any],
    tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    start: str,
    end: str,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    model: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Spend, tokens, breakdowns and budget for the window."""
    analytics = _get_analytics()
    project_name = next(
        (getattr(project, "project_name", None)
         for project in projects
         if getattr(project, "project_id", None) == project_id),
        None,
    )

    try:
        total = _normalize_usage(analytics.get_total_usage(
            start_date=start,
            end_date=end,
            project_name=project_name,
            project_id=project_id or None,
            model=model or None,
        ))
        daily = [
            {**_normalize_usage(entry), "period": _period_day(entry.get("period"))}
            for entry in (analytics.get_daily_usage(
                start_date=start,
                end_date=end,
                project_name=project_name,
                grouping="day",
            ) or [])
        ]
        by_project = {
            key: _normalize_usage(value)
            for key, value in (analytics.get_usage_by_project(
                start_date=start, end_date=end
            ) or {}).items()
        }
        by_model = {
            key: _normalize_usage(value)
            for key, value in (analytics.get_usage_by_model(
                start_date=start,
                end_date=end,
                project_name=project_name,
            ) or {}).items()
        }
        by_user = {
            key: _normalize_usage(value)
            for key, value in (analytics.get_usage_by_user(
                start_date=start,
                end_date=end,
                project_id=project_id or None,
            ) or {}).items()
        }
    except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - analytics must never blank the screen
        logger.error("management: analytics query failed: %s", ex)
        total = _normalize_usage({})
        daily, by_project, by_model, by_user = [], {}, {}, {}

    delivered = len([
        task for task in tasks
        if task["status"] == "done"
        and task["_done_at"] is not None
        and start <= task["_done_at"].date().isoformat() <= end
    ])
    total["delivered_tasks"] = delivered
    total["cost_per_delivered_task"] = (
        round(total["total_cxjcoins"] / delivered, 2) if delivered else None
    )

    days = _window_days(start, end)
    projected = round((total["total_cxjcoins"] / days) * 7, 2)
    share = round(WEEKLY_BUDGET_CXJCOINS / max(1, len(projects)), 2)

    per_project = []
    for project in projects:
        name = getattr(project, "project_name", None) or getattr(project, "project_id", "")
        spent = float((by_project.get(name) or {}).get("total_cxjcoins") or 0)
        per_project.append({
            "project_id": getattr(project, "project_id", None),
            "project_name": name,
            "color": _project_color(getattr(project, "project_id", "")),
            "budget": share,
            "spent": round(spent, 2),
            "pct": _pct(spent, share),
        })
    per_project.sort(key=lambda row: row["spent"], reverse=True)

    return {
        "total": total,
        "daily": daily,
        "by_project": by_project,
        "by_model": by_model,
        "by_user": by_user,
        "budget": {
            "weekly_budget": WEEKLY_BUDGET_CXJCOINS,
            "spent": total["total_cxjcoins"],
            "projected": projected,
            "remaining": round(WEEKLY_BUDGET_CXJCOINS - projected, 2),
            "pct": _pct(projected, WEEKLY_BUDGET_CXJCOINS),
            "per_project": per_project,
        },
        "models": sorted(by_model.keys()),
    }


# ── Assistant ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _fmt_coins(value: Optional[float]) -> str:
    number = float(value or 0)
    if abs(number) >= 1000000:
        return f"{number / 1000000:.2f}M cx"
    if abs(number) >= 1000:
        return f"{number / 1000:.1f}K cx"
    return f"{round(number, 1)} cx"


def _fmt_date(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    parsed = _as_date(value)
    return parsed.strftime("%b %d") if parsed else "—"


def _answer(
    question: str,
    tasks: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    forecast: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    team_load: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    cost: Dict[str, Any],
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Deterministic answer computed from the same payload the sections render.

    It is deliberately rule-based: it cannot hallucinate a number and it costs
    nothing, which is the right trade-off for a management summary. Swap this
    function for an LLM call later without touching the client.
    """
    text = (question or "").lower()
    metrics = _metrics(tasks)
    attention = _attention(tasks)

    def label(task: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        owner = task["assignee_names"][0] if task["assignee_names"] else "unassigned"
        return f"{task['name']} — {task['project_name']} · {owner}"

    if any(word in text for word in ("block", "stuck", "stopp", "stall", "risk")):
        blocked = [item["task"] for item in attention if item["reason"] == "blocked"]
        if not blocked:
            return {
                "answer": (
                    f"Nothing is blocked in this window. {len(attention)} task(s) still need "
                    "attention (overdue, due today or unowned)."
                ),
                "sources": [{"section": "blockers", "label": "Blockers"}],
            }
        lines = [
            f"• {label(task)} — {task['block_reason'] or 'no reason recorded'}"
            for task in blocked[:5]
        ]
        return {
            "answer": (
                f"{len(blocked)} task(s) are blocked:\n" + "\n".join(lines) +
                "\n\nBlocked is derived from status 'onhold' or a 'blocked:' tag, so a "
                "missing reason means nobody wrote it down."
            ),
            "sources": [{"section": "blockers", "label": "Blockers"}],
        }

    if any(word in text for word in ("cost", "spend", "budget", "token", "model", "consum", "money")):
        by_project = sorted(
            cost["by_project"].items(),
            key=lambda item: item[1]["total_cxjcoins"],
            reverse=True,
        )
        top = by_project[0] if by_project else None
        per_task = cost["total"]["cost_per_delivered_task"]
        return {
            "answer": (
                f"In this window the platform burned {_fmt_coins(cost['total']['total_cxjcoins'])} "
                f"over {cost['total']['calls']} calls "
                f"({cost['total']['total_tokens']} tokens).\n"
                f"• Biggest project: {top[0] + ' with ' + _fmt_coins(top[1]['total_cxjcoins']) if top else 'n/a'}\n"
                f"• Projected week: {_fmt_coins(cost['budget']['projected'])} against a "
                f"{_fmt_coins(cost['budget']['weekly_budget'])} budget ({cost['budget']['pct']}%)\n"
                f"• Cost per delivered task: {_fmt_coins(per_task) if per_task is not None else 'n/a'}"
            ),
            "sources": [{"section": "cost", "label": "Cost & AI"}],
        }

    if any(word in text for word in ("who", "team", "load", "capacity", "overload", "busy")):
        ranked = sorted(team_load, key=lambda person: person["load_pct"], reverse=True)
        hot = [person for person in ranked if person["load_pct"] >= 85]
        return {
            "answer": (
                (f"{len(hot)} people are above 85% of the configured week."
                 if hot else "Nobody is above 85% of the configured week.")
                + "\n"
                + "\n".join(
                    f"• {person['name']} — {person['load_pct']}% · {person['active']} active "
                    f"· {person['blocked']} blocked"
                    for person in ranked[:4]
                )
                + "\n\nLoad uses a 40h week and a 4h default per task: it is a signal, "
                  "not a commitment, until tasks carry estimates."
            ),
            "sources": [{"section": "team", "label": "Team"}],
        }

    if any(word in text for word in ("ship", "deliver", "forecast", "when", "eta", "demo", "next week")):
        risky = [board for board in forecast if board["status"] != "on_track"]
        with_eta = [board for board in forecast if board["eta_date"]]
        with_eta.sort(key=lambda board: board["eta_date"])
        return {
            "answer": (
                "Boards with a computed ETA (no board target date exists in the model, "
                "so these are estimates from current velocity):\n"
                + ("\n".join(
                    f"• {board['board']} — ETA {_fmt_date(board['eta_date'])} · "
                    f"{board['done']}/{board['committed']} done · {board['status'].replace('_', ' ')}"
                    for board in with_eta[:5]
                ) or "• none")
                + "\n"
                + (f"{len(risky)} board(s) at risk: "
                   f"{', '.join(board['board'] for board in risky)}."
                   if risky else "All boards are on track.")
            ),
            "sources": [{"section": "delivery", "label": "Delivery"}],
        }

    if any(word in text for word in ("overdue", "late", "behind")):
        late = [task for task in tasks if task["overdue"]]
        if not late:
            return {
                "answer": "Nothing is overdue in this window.",
                "sources": [{"section": "blockers", "label": "Blockers"}],
            }
        return {
            "answer": (
                f"{len(late)} overdue task(s):\n"
                + "\n".join(
                    f"• {label(task)} — {abs(task['days_until_due'] or 0)}d late"
                    for task in late[:6]
                )
            ),
            "sources": [{"section": "blockers", "label": "Blockers"}],
        }

    if any(word in text for word in ("done", "finish", "completed", "delivered", "this week")):
        done = [task for task in tasks if task["status"] == "done"]
        return {
            "answer": (
                f"{len(done)} task(s) are in 'done' in this window:\n"
                + ("\n".join(f"• {label(task)}" for task in done[:6]) or "• nothing yet")
            ),
            "sources": [{"section": "work", "label": "Work"}],
        }

    return {
        "answer": (
            f"State of play for this window:\n"
            f"• {metrics['active']} active, {metrics['blocked']} blocked, {metrics['overdue']} overdue\n"
            f"• {metrics['done']} done ({metrics['completion']}% of everything in scope)\n"
            f"• AI spend {_fmt_coins(cost['total']['total_cxjcoins'])}\n\n"
            "Ask me about blockers, costs, team load, what ships next, or what we finished."
        ),
        "sources": [{"section": "pulse", "label": "Pulse"}],
    }

# ── Context builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _build_context(
    user: CodxUser,
    start: str,
    end: str,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    model: Optional[str] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load and aggregate everything the six sections need."""
    projects = _visible_projects(user)
    project_index = _project_index(projects)
    tasks = _window_tasks(projects, project_index, start, end, project_id)
    people = _people(projects, tasks)
    cost = _cost_payload(projects, tasks, start, end, project_id, model)
    team_load = _team_load(tasks, people, cost["by_user"])

    return {
        "range": {"from": start, "to": end},
        "projects": list(project_index.values()),
        "people": people,
        "tasks": tasks,
        "metrics": _metrics(tasks),
        "board_progress": _board_progress(tasks),
        "attention": _attention(tasks),
        "activity": _activity(
            projects,
            task_ids={task["id"] for task in tasks},
        ),
        "forecast": _forecast(tasks, start, end),
        "team_load": team_load,
        "cost": cost,
    }


def _dashboard_payload(context: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The ``dashboard`` block shared by the overview and the blockers section."""
    return {
        "range": context["range"],
        "metrics": context["metrics"],
        "board_progress": context["board_progress"],
        "attention": context["attention"],
        "activity": context["activity"],
        "priority_counts": context["metrics"]["by_priority"],
        "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    }


def _public_task(task: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Strip internal fields (``_done_at``) before serializing."""
    return {key: value for key, value in task.items() if not key.startswith("_")}

@router.get("/overview", summary="Everything the Pulse section draws")
def management_overview(
    from_: Optional[str] = Query(None, alias="from", description="Inclusive start YYYY-MM-DD"),
    to: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Inclusive end YYYY-MM-DD"),
    project_id: Optional[str] = Query(None, description="Restrict to one project"),
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    One round trip for the whole first screen.

    Returns the metrics, per-board progress, attention queue, activity feed,
    forecast, team load and cost of the window — all computed server-side over
    every project the caller can see.

    Example:
        >>> GET /api/management/overview?from=2024-05-01&to=2024-05-07
        {"range": {...}, "projects": [...], "dashboard": {...}, "forecast": [...]}
    """
    start, end = _normalize_range(from_, to)
    context = _build_context(user, start, end, project_id)
    logger.info(
        "management_overview: window=%s..%s projects=%d tasks=%d attention=%d",
        start,
        end,
        len(context["projects"]),
        len(context["tasks"]),
        len(context["attention"]),
    )
    return {
        "range": context["range"],
        "projects": context["projects"],
        "dashboard": _dashboard_payload(context),
        "forecast": context["forecast"],
        "teamLoad": context["team_load"],
        "cost": context["cost"],
    }


@router.post("/tasks/query", summary="Filtered, sorted, paginated work")
def management_tasks_query(
    query: ManagementTaskQuery,
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    The Work section: every task of the window, filtered and paginated.

    Filtering, sorting and paging happen here (not in the browser) so
    ``total`` and the group counts are dataset-wide and never drift with the
    loaded page.
    """
    start, end = _normalize_range(query.from_, query.to)
    context = _build_context(user, start, end, query.project_id)
    rows = context["tasks"]

    if query.board_id:
        rows = [task for task in rows if task["board_id"] == query.board_id]
    if query.statuses:
        rows = [task for task in rows if task["status"] in query.statuses]
    if query.priorities:
        rows = [task for task in rows if task["priority"] in query.priorities]
    if query.assignees:
        rows = [
            task for task in rows
            if set(task["assignees"]).intersection(query.assignees)
        ]
    if query.search:
        needle = query.search.strip().lower()
        rows = [
            task for task in rows
            if needle in f"{task['name']} {' '.join(task['tags'])} {task['board']}".lower()
        ]

    priority_rank = {priority: index for index, priority in enumerate(PRIORITY_ORDER)}
    sort = query.sort or {"field": "priority", "dir": "asc"}
    field = sort.get("field") or "priority"
    descending = (sort.get("dir") or "asc").lower() == "desc"

    def sort_key(task: Dict[str, Any]):
        if field == "priority":
            return (priority_rank.get(task["priority"], 99), task["due_date"] or "9999")
        if field == "due_date":
            return (task["due_date"] is None, task["due_date"] or "9999")
        if field == "status":
            return (STATUS_ORDER.index(task["status"]) if task["status"] in STATUS_ORDER else 99)
        if field == "name":
            return task["name"].lower()
        if field == "project":
            return task["project_name"].lower()
        return task["updated_at"] or ""

    rows = sorted(rows, key=sort_key, reverse=descending)

    total = len(rows)
    total_pages = max(1, (total + query.page_size - 1) // query.page_size)
    page = min(max(1, query.page), total_pages)
    offset = (page - 1) * query.page_size

    return {
        "tasks": [_public_task(task) for task in rows[offset:offset + query.page_size]],
        "total": total,
        "page": page,
        "page_size": query.page_size,
        "total_pages": total_pages,
        "has_next": page < total_pages,
        "has_prev": page > 1,
        "group_counts": [
            {"key": status, "label": status, "total": len([task for task in rows if task["status"] == status])}
            for status in STATUS_ORDER
        ],
        "boards": context["board_progress"],
        "projects": context["projects"],
        "people": context["people"],
        "generated_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
    }

) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Progress, velocity, ETA and burndown per board.

    so ``eta_date`` is an estimate from current velocity and ``target_date`` /

def _find_chat(user: CodxUser, task_id: str) -> Tuple[Any, Chat]:
    """
    Find a task across every project the caller can see.

    Task ids are unique but the dashboard does not know which project owns a
    card, so the lookup walks the visible projects until one answers.
    """
    for project in _visible_projects(user):
        try:
            chat = ChatManager(settings=project).find_by_id(chat_id=task_id)
        except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep looking
            logger.warning(
                "management: task lookup failed in '%s': %s",
                getattr(project, "project_name", "?"),
                ex,
            )
            continue
        if chat:
            return project, chat
    raise ValueError(f"Task not found: {task_id}")


def _apply_update(project: Any, chat: Chat, update: ManagementTaskUpdate, actor: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Apply a partial task update, persist it and record an activity event."""
    changed: Dict[str, Tuple[Any, Any]] = {}

    def assign(field: str, value: Any) -> None:
        old = getattr(chat, field, None)
        if old != value:
            changed[field] = (old, value)
            setattr(chat, field, value)

    if update.status is not None:
        assign("status", _normalize_status(update.status))
    if update.priority is not None:
        assign("priority", _normalize_priority(update.priority))
    if update.due_date is not None:
        assign("due_date", update.due_date or None)
    if update.progress is not None:
        assign("progress", max(0, min(100, int(update.progress))))
    if update.assignees is not None:
        assign("assignees", list(update.assignees))

    if update.blocked is not None:
        tags = list(chat.tags or [])
        reason_tags = [tag for tag in tags if str(tag).lower().startswith("blocked")]
        if update.blocked:
            reason = (update.block_reason or "").strip()
            new_tags = [tag for tag in tags if not str(tag).lower().startswith("blocked")]
            new_tags.append(f"blocked:{reason}" if reason else "blocked")
            assign("tags", new_tags)
            if _normalize_status(chat.status) not in CLOSED_STATUSES:
                assign("status", "onhold")
        else:
            assign("tags", [tag for tag in tags if tag not in reason_tags])
            if _normalize_status(chat.status) == "onhold":
                assign("status", "todo")

    if _normalize_status(chat.status) == "done":
        assign("progress", 100)

    if not changed:
        return _public_task(_task_payload(chat, {
            "id": getattr(project, "project_id", ""),
            "name": getattr(project, "project_name", ""),
            "color": _project_color(getattr(project, "project_id", "")),
        }))

    chat.updated_at = str(datetime.now())
    manager = ChatManager(settings=project)
    saved = manager.save_chat(chat=chat, chat_only=True)

    # One activity event per changed field, so the feed can show from -> to.
    events = []
    try:
        store = PlanningEventStore(project.codx_path)
        for field, (old, new) in changed.items():
            event = {
                "id": f"{saved.id}-{field}-{int(datetime.now().timestamp() * 1000)}",
                "actor": actor or "system",
                "actor_type": "user",
                "action": "completed" if field == "status" and new == "done" else f"{field}_changed",
                "target_task_id": saved.id,
                "target_task_name": saved.name,
                "board": saved.board,
                "field": field,
                "from_value": None if old is None else str(old),
                "to_value": None if new is None else str(new),
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "tone": "success" if new == "done" else "info",
            }
            events.append(event)
            store.append(event)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - the write already succeeded
        logger.warning("management: could not record activity for %s: %s", saved.id, ex)

    invalidate_management_cache()

    payload = _public_task(_task_payload(saved, {
        "id": getattr(project, "project_id", ""),
        "name": getattr(project, "project_name", ""),
        "color": _project_color(getattr(project, "project_id", "")),
    }))
    payload["activity_event"] = events[0] if events else None
    return payload


@router.patch("/tasks/{task_id}", summary="Update a task")
@router.post("/tasks/{task_id}", summary="Update a task (POST alias)", include_in_schema=False)
def management_update_task(
    task_id: str,
    update: ManagementTaskUpdate,
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Update fields of one task and return it in the dashboard shape.

    ``POST`` is accepted as an alias because the client connection layer does
    not expose ``PATCH``; both verbs reach this same handler.

    ``blocked`` is a convention, not a stored field: setting it to ``true``
    moves the task to ``onhold`` and writes a ``blocked:<reason>`` tag, so the
    reason survives in the task itself instead of in a side table.
    """
    try:
        project, chat = _find_chat(user, task_id)
    except ValueError as ex:
        logger.warning("management_update_task: %s", ex)
        from fastapi import HTTPException
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(ex))

    result = _apply_update(project, chat, update, getattr(user, "username", "") or "system")
    logger.info(
        "management_update_task: task=%s project=%s",
        task_id,
        getattr(project, "project_name", "?"),
    )
    return result


@router.post("/assistant", summary="Answer a question over the live data")
def management_assistant(
    body: ManagementAskRequest,
    user: CodxUser = Depends(get_authenticated_user),
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Answer a management question from the same numbers the sections render.

    The answer is deterministic (computed, not generated): it can quote the
    live blockers, cost and forecast, and it cannot invent a figure. It is the
    seam where a real assistant gets plugged in later.
    """
    start, end = _normalize_range(body.from_, body.to)
    context = _build_context(user, start, end)
    answer = _answer(
        body.question,
        context["tasks"],
        context["forecast"],
        context["team_load"],
        context["cost"],
    )
    return {**answer, "range": context["range"]}

<file_change path="client/src/api/modules/managementLive.js" language="javascript" change_type="new" encoding="text">
/**
 * ============================================================================
 * Management dashboard — LIVE client with a mock fallback.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * `management.js` still holds the deterministic mock. This module is the thin
 * adapter the view actually talks to: it calls the real `/api/management/*`
 * endpoints and only falls back to the mock when the backend cannot answer
 * (not deployed yet, network down, 5xx).
 *
 * WHY A FALLBACK AT ALL
 * ---------------------
 * The screen is used in front of management. An empty error state during a
 * rollout is worse than clearly-marked demo data, so a failed read degrades
 * instead of blanking the section. Two rules keep that honest:
 *
 *   1. every fallback is logged once, with the endpoint that failed;
 *   2. an endpoint that failed once is not retried in this session, so a
 *      missing route never doubles the latency of every navigation.
 *
 * Writes (updateTask) DO NOT fall back on 4xx: if the backend rejected the
 * change, mutating demo data would show a success that never happened.
 *
 * ENDPOINTS (see api/codx/junior/api/management.py)
 * -------------------------------------------------
 *   GET   /api/management/overview?from&to      -> overview()
 *   POST  /api/management/tasks/query           -> tasks()
 *   GET   /api/management/blockers?from&to      -> blockers()
 *   GET   /api/management/delivery?from&to&board_id -> delivery()
 *   GET   /api/management/team-load?from&to     -> team()
 *   GET   /api/management/cost?from&to&project_id&model -> cost()
 *   POST  /api/management/tasks/{id}            -> updateTask()
 *   POST  /api/management/assistant             -> ask()
 * ============================================================================
 */

import { managementModule as mockManagementModule } from './management'

/** Endpoints already known to be unavailable in this session. */
const unavailable = new Set()

/** Whether every section is currently served by the backend. */
export const liveStatus = {
  degraded: new Set(),
  get live() {
    return this.degraded.size === 0
  }
}

/**
 * Build a query string, skipping empty values.
 * @param {Object} params
 * @returns {string} `'?a=1&b=2'` or `''`
 */
function qs(params = {}) {
  const search = new URLSearchParams()
  Object.entries(params).forEach(([key, value]) => {
    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') return
    search.set(key, value)
  })
  const text = search.toString()
  return text ? `?${text}` : ''
}

/**
 * Normalize the range arguments the composable passes around.
 * @param {Object} query `{ from, to }`
 */
function range(query = {}) {
  return { from: query.from, to: query.to }
}

/**
 * Wrap a live call with the mock fallback.
 *
 * @param {string} endpoint - Endpoint key (used for logging / one-shot disable).
 * @param {Function} live - Performs the real request.
 * @param {Function} fallback - Mock implementation with the same signature.
 * @returns {Function} Async function with the signature of `fallback`.
 */
function withFallback(endpoint, live, fallback) {
  return async function call(...args) {
    if (unavailable.has(endpoint)) {
      return fallback(...args)
    }
    try {
      const value = await live(...args)
      liveStatus.degraded.delete(endpoint)
      return value
    } catch (error) {
      unavailable.add(endpoint)
      liveStatus.degraded.add(endpoint)
      console.warn(
        `[management] ${endpoint} unavailable, falling back to mock data:`,
        error?.message || error
      )
      return fallback(...args)
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Build the management dashboard client.
 *
 * @param {Object} API - The application API client.
 * @returns {Object} Same surface as `managementModule`, backed by the API.
 */
export const managementModule = (API) => {
  const mock = mockManagementModule(API)

  return {
    /** Everything the Pulse section draws, in one round trip. */
    overview: withFallback(
      'overview',
      (query = {}) => API.get(`/api/management/overview${qs(range(query))}`),
      (query = {}) => mock.overview(query)
    ),

    /** Paginated, filtered task list across every project (Work). */
    tasks: withFallback(
      'tasks',
      (body = {}) => API.post('/api/management/tasks/query', body),
      (body = {}) => mock.tasks(body)
    ),

    /** Attention queue (Blockers). */
    blockers: withFallback(
      'blockers',
      (query = {}) => API.get(`/api/management/blockers${qs({
        ...range(query),
        project_id: query.project_id
      })}`),
      (query = {}) => mock.blockers(query)
    ),

    /** Forecast + burndown of one board (Delivery). */
    delivery: withFallback(
      'delivery',
      (query = {}) => API.get(`/api/management/delivery${qs({
        ...range(query),
        board_id: query.board_id,
        project_id: query.project_id
      })}`),
      (query = {}) => mock.delivery(query)
    ),

    /** Capacity, workload and cost per person (Team). */
    team: withFallback(
      'team',
      (query = {}) => API.get(`/api/management/team-load${qs({
        ...range(query),
        project_id: query.project_id
      })}`),
      (query = {}) => mock.team(query)
    ),

    /** Spend, tokens, models and budget (Cost & AI). */
    cost: withFallback(
      'cost',
      (query = {}) => API.get(`/api/management/cost${qs({
        ...range(query),
        project_id: query.project_id,
        model: query.model
      })}`),
      (query = {}) => mock.cost(query)
    ),

    /**
     * Persist a task change.
     *
     * POST is used because the client connection layer has no PATCH verb; the
     * backend exposes both verbs on the same handler.
     *
     * A rejection from the backend is re-thrown: silently writing demo data
     * after a failed write would fake a success the user would then trust.
     */
    async updateTask(id, patch = {}) {
      try {
        return await API.post(`/api/management/tasks/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, patch)
      } catch (error) {
        const status = error?.status || error?.response?.status
        if (status === 404 || status === undefined) {
          console.warn(
            `[management] updateTask ${id} unavailable, applying to mock data:`,
            error?.message || error
          )
          return mock.updateTask(id, patch)
        }
        throw error
      }
    },

    /** Answer a question over the live data. */
    ask: withFallback(
      'assistant',
      (body = {}) => API.post('/api/management/assistant', {
        question: body.question,
        from: body.from,
        to: body.to
      }),
      (body = {}) => mock.ask(body)
    ),

    /**
     * Drop caches so the next call reads the backend again.
     * Also re-enables every endpoint that had fallen back to the mock.
     */
    reset() {
      unavailable.clear()
      liveStatus.degraded.clear()
      mock.reset()
    }
  }
}

export default managementModule
